nodes.title: Does P = NP?
nodes.spec:
Does P = NP?

Decide whether every problem whose solutions can be checked in polynomial time can also be solved in polynomial time. Lean decides what is proven: a node is proven only when its frozen statement checks against the pinned Mathlib.

nodes.title: Foundations: machines, P, NP and Cook-Levin
nodes.spec:
Foundations: machines, P, NP and Cook-Levin

Fix the ground every other program stands on: P and NP over binary words on Mathlib's TM2 machines, polynomial-time reductions, SAT, and Cook-Levin, which makes SAT the one problem the whole question turns on.

nodes.title: Lower bounds: toward P ≠ NP
nodes.spec:
Lower bounds: toward P ≠ NP

Aim at P ≠ NP from below with circuit lower bounds. A superpolynomial circuit lower bound for an NP problem separates P from NP; the known bounds are for restricted circuits (monotone, constant depth), and the barriers program says why their methods stop there.

nodes.title: Barriers: relativization, natural proofs, algebrization
nodes.spec:
Barriers: relativization, natural proofs, algebrization

Theorems about proofs: no argument that relativizes, is natural, or algebrizes can settle P vs NP. Formalize them, and use them to end lines of attack as dead ends with the reason.

nodes.title: Upper bounds: toward P = NP
nodes.spec:
Upper bounds: toward P = NP

Aim at P = NP from above: polynomial algorithms for restricted SAT, Schaefer's dichotomy for which Boolean constraint problems are easy, and claimed algorithms for SAT refuted by checked counterexamples.

nodes.title: Polynomial-time functions compose
nodes.spec:
Polynomial-time functions compose

A polynomial-time function followed by another is polynomial time.

```lean
∀ f g : Word → Word, PolyTime f → PolyTime g → PolyTime (g ∘ f)
```
nodes.statement: ∀ f g : Word → Word, PolyTime f → PolyTime g → PolyTime (g ∘ f)

nodes.title: P is contained in NP
nodes.spec:
P is contained in NP

Every language decided in polynomial time has polynomial-time checkable certificates (the empty one).

```lean
∀ L : Lang, InP L → InNP L
```
nodes.statement: ∀ L : Lang, InP L → InNP L

nodes.title: Reductions are transitive
nodes.spec:
Reductions are transitive

If A reduces to B and B to C in polynomial time, then A reduces to C.

```lean
∀ A B C : Lang, PolyReduces A B → PolyReduces B C → PolyReduces A C
```
nodes.statement: ∀ A B C : Lang, PolyReduces A B → PolyReduces B C → PolyReduces A C

nodes.title: P is closed under reductions
nodes.spec:
P is closed under reductions

A language that reduces to one in P is in P.

```lean
∀ A B : Lang, PolyReduces A B → InP B → InP A
```
nodes.statement: ∀ A B : Lang, PolyReduces A B → InP B → InP A

nodes.title: NP is closed under reductions
nodes.spec:
NP is closed under reductions

A language that reduces to one in NP is in NP.

```lean
∀ A B : Lang, PolyReduces A B → InNP B → InNP A
```
nodes.statement: ∀ A B : Lang, PolyReduces A B → InNP B → InNP A

nodes.title: SAT is in NP
nodes.spec:
SAT is in NP

A satisfying assignment is a certificate that a CNF formula is satisfiable, checkable in polynomial time.

```lean
InNP SAT
```
nodes.statement: InNP SAT

nodes.title: Cook-Levin: SAT is NP-complete
nodes.spec:
Cook-Levin: SAT is NP-complete

Every NP language reduces to SAT in polynomial time, by encoding an accepting run of its verifier as a CNF formula.

```lean
NPComplete SAT
```
nodes.statement: NPComplete SAT

nodes.title: P = NP exactly when SAT is in P
nodes.spec:
P = NP exactly when SAT is in P

With Cook-Levin, the whole question is whether one problem, SAT, has a polynomial algorithm.

```lean
PEqNP ↔ InP SAT
```
nodes.statement: PEqNP ↔ InP SAT

nodes.title: 3-SAT is NP-complete
nodes.spec:
3-SAT is NP-complete

Clauses of at most three literals are already as hard as SAT.

```lean
NPComplete ThreeSAT
```
nodes.statement: NPComplete ThreeSAT

nodes.title: Oracle machines with no oracle decide exactly P
nodes.spec:
Oracle machines with no oracle decide exactly P

The oracle machine model the barriers program uses agrees with Mathlib's TM2 model when the oracle is empty.

```lean
∀ L : Lang, InP L ↔ InPO ∅ L
```
nodes.statement: ∀ L : Lang, InP L ↔ InPO ∅ L

nodes.title: Most Boolean functions need large circuits (Shannon)
nodes.spec:
Most Boolean functions need large circuits (Shannon)

Counting circuits against functions: for large n some function of n inputs needs fan-in-two circuits of size about 2^n / n.

```lean
∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∃ f : BoolFn n, 2 ^ n ≤ 10 * n * circuitSize n f
```
nodes.statement: ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∃ f : BoolFn n, 2 ^ n ≤ 10 * n * circuitSize n f

nodes.title: Monotone circuits compute monotone functions
nodes.spec:
Monotone circuits compute monotone functions

A circuit with no negations computes a monotone function: turning inputs on never turns the output off.

```lean
∀ (c : Circuit) (n : ℕ), c.Monotone → Monotone fun x : Fin n → Bool => c.eval (extend x)
```
nodes.statement: ∀ (c : Circuit) (n : ℕ), c.Monotone → Monotone fun x : Fin n → Bool => c.eval (extend x)

nodes.title: Switching lemma (Håstad, in counting form)
nodes.spec:
Switching lemma (Håstad, in counting form)

A random restriction leaving ℓ of n variables free collapses a width-w DNF to a shallow decision tree, except for a (10ℓw/n)^t fraction of restrictions.

```lean
∀ (n w t ℓ : ℕ) (F : DNF n), F.width ≤ w → ((badRestrictions F ℓ t).card : ℝ) ≤ ((10 * ℓ * w : ℝ) / n) ^ t * (restrictions n ℓ).card
```
nodes.statement: ∀ (n w t ℓ : ℕ) (F : DNF n), F.width ≤ w → ((badRestrictions F ℓ t).card : ℝ) ≤ ((10 * ℓ * w : ℝ) / n) ^ t * (restrictions n ℓ).card

nodes.title: Håstad's bound: parity needs exponential size at constant depth
nodes.spec:
Håstad's bound: parity needs exponential size at constant depth

Depth-d unbounded fan-in circuits for parity on n inputs have size at least 2^(n^(1/(d-1))/10) for large n.

```lean
∀ d : ℕ, 2 ≤ d → ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∀ c : Circuit, c.depth ≤ d → Computes c n (parity n) → (2 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / ((d : ℝ) - 1)) / 10) ≤ c.size
```
nodes.statement: ∀ d : ℕ, 2 ≤ d → ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∀ c : Circuit, c.depth ≤ d → Computes c n (parity n) → (2 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / ((d : ℝ) - 1)) / 10) ≤ c.size

nodes.title: Parity is not in AC0
nodes.spec:
Parity is not in AC0

No family of constant-depth, polynomial-size circuits computes parity.

```lean
¬ InAC0 parity
```
nodes.statement: ¬ InAC0 parity

nodes.title: Monotone circuits for clique need exponential size (Razborov, Alon-Boppana)
nodes.spec:
Monotone circuits for clique need exponential size (Razborov, Alon-Boppana)

Monotone fan-in-two circuits that detect a clique of size about m^(1/4) in an m-vertex graph have size 2^(Ω(m^(1/8))).

```lean
∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∃ m₀ : ℕ, ∀ m ≥ m₀, ∀ c : Circuit, c.Monotone → c.FanInTwo → Computes c (m * m) (clique m (Nat.sqrt (Nat.sqrt m))) → (2 : ℝ) ^ (ε * (m : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 8)) ≤ c.size
```
nodes.statement: ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∃ m₀ : ℕ, ∀ m ≥ m₀, ∀ c : Circuit, c.Monotone → c.FanInTwo → Computes c (m * m) (clique m (Nat.sqrt (Nat.sqrt m))) → (2 : ℝ) ^ (ε * (m : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 8)) ≤ c.size

nodes.title: P is not NP
nodes.spec:
P is not NP

The program's target: some language in NP has no polynomial-time decider.

```lean
¬ PEqNP
```
nodes.statement: ¬ PEqNP

nodes.title: An oracle that makes P equal NP (Baker-Gill-Solovay)
nodes.spec:
An oracle that makes P equal NP (Baker-Gill-Solovay)

Relative to a PSPACE-complete oracle, every NP language is in P.

```lean
∃ A : Lang, ∀ L : Lang, InNPO A L → InPO A L
```
nodes.statement: ∃ A : Lang, ∀ L : Lang, InNPO A L → InPO A L

nodes.title: An oracle that separates P from NP (Baker-Gill-Solovay)
nodes.spec:
An oracle that separates P from NP (Baker-Gill-Solovay)

A diagonal oracle puts a language in NP relative to it but not in P relative to it.

```lean
∃ B L : Lang, InNPO B L ∧ ¬ InPO B L
```
nodes.statement: ∃ B L : Lang, InNPO B L ∧ ¬ InPO B L

nodes.title: Hard functions are most functions (largeness)
nodes.spec:
Hard functions are most functions (largeness)

At least half of all functions of n inputs need circuits of size about 2^n / n, so a property that holds for hard functions is large.

```lean
∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, 2 ^ 2 ^ n ≤ 2 * {f : BoolFn n | 2 ^ n ≤ 10 * n * circuitSize n f}.ncard
```
nodes.statement: ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, 2 ^ 2 ^ n ≤ 2 * {f : BoolFn n | 2 ^ n ≤ 10 * n * circuitSize n f}.ncard

nodes.title: Large properties useful against small circuits reject every small generator (Razborov-Rudich, core)
nodes.spec:
Large properties useful against small circuits reject every small generator (Razborov-Rudich, core)

A property that holds for many functions and for no small circuit tells the outputs of any small-circuit generator from random functions.

```lean
∀ (Γ : ∀ n, Set (BoolFn n)) (k c : ℕ), (∀ n ≥ c, (2 : ℝ) ^ 2 ^ n ≤ 2 ^ (c * n) * (Γ n).ncard) → (∀ n ≥ c, ∀ f ∈ Γ n, n ^ k < circuitSize n f) → ∀ n ≥ c, ∀ (m : ℕ) (g : (Fin m → Bool) → BoolFn n), (∀ s, circuitSize n (g s) ≤ n ^ k) → ∃ D : Set (BoolFn n), (∀ s, g s ∉ D) ∧ (2 : ℝ) ^ 2 ^ n ≤ 2 ^ (c * n) * D.ncard
```
nodes.statement: ∀ (Γ : ∀ n, Set (BoolFn n)) (k c : ℕ), (∀ n ≥ c, (2 : ℝ) ^ 2 ^ n ≤ 2 ^ (c * n) * (Γ n).ncard) → (∀ n ≥ c, ∀ f ∈ Γ n, n ^ k < circuitSize n f) → ∀ n ≥ c, ∀ (m : ℕ) (g : (Fin m → Bool) → BoolFn n), (∀ s, circuitSize n (g s) ≤ n ^ k) → ∃ D : Set (BoolFn n), (∀ s, g s ∉ D) ∧ (2 : ℝ) ^ 2 ^ n ≤ 2 ^ (c * n) * D.ncard

nodes.title: An algebraic oracle under which NP is in P (Aaronson-Wigderson)
nodes.spec:
An algebraic oracle under which NP is in P (Aaronson-Wigderson)

There is an oracle A with a multilinear extension Ã such that NP relative to Ã is in P relative to A.

```lean
∃ (A : Lang) (E : AlgExt A), ∀ L : Lang, InNPO E.oracle L → InPO A L
```
nodes.statement: ∃ (A : Lang) (E : AlgExt A), ∀ L : Lang, InNPO E.oracle L → InPO A L

nodes.title: An algebraic oracle under which NP is not in P (Aaronson-Wigderson)
nodes.spec:
An algebraic oracle under which NP is not in P (Aaronson-Wigderson)

There is an oracle A with a multilinear extension Ã such that some language in NP relative to A is not in P relative to Ã.

```lean
∃ (A : Lang) (E : AlgExt A) (L : Lang), InNPO A L ∧ ¬ InPO E.oracle L
```
nodes.statement: ∃ (A : Lang) (E : AlgExt A) (L : Lang), InNPO A L ∧ ¬ InPO E.oracle L

nodes.title: 2-SAT is in P
nodes.spec:
2-SAT is in P

Satisfiability of clauses with at most two literals is decided in polynomial time through the implication graph.

```lean
InP TwoSAT
```
nodes.statement: InP TwoSAT

nodes.title: Horn-SAT is in P
nodes.spec:
Horn-SAT is in P

Satisfiability of clauses with at most one positive literal is decided in polynomial time by unit propagation.

```lean
InP HornSAT
```
nodes.statement: InP HornSAT

nodes.title: Schaefer's dichotomy: the six tractable classes are in P
nodes.spec:
Schaefer's dichotomy: the six tractable classes are in P

A Boolean constraint language that is 0-valid, 1-valid, Horn, dual Horn, bijunctive or affine has a polynomial-time CSP.

```lean
∀ Γ : ConstraintLang, Schaefer Γ → InP (CSP Γ)
```
nodes.statement: ∀ Γ : ConstraintLang, Schaefer Γ → InP (CSP Γ)

nodes.title: Schaefer's dichotomy: every other constraint language is NP-complete
nodes.spec:
Schaefer's dichotomy: every other constraint language is NP-complete

Outside Schaefer's six classes, the Boolean CSP is NP-complete.

```lean
∀ Γ : ConstraintLang, ¬ Schaefer Γ → NPComplete (CSP Γ)
```
nodes.statement: ∀ Γ : ConstraintLang, ¬ Schaefer Γ → NPComplete (CSP Γ)

nodes.title: Majority vote is not a SAT algorithm (checked counterexample)
nodes.spec:
Majority vote is not a SAT algorithm (checked counterexample)

Setting each variable to its more frequent sign fails on a satisfiable formula; the counterexample is checked in Lean.

```lean
∃ φ : CNF, φ.Satisfiable ∧ φ.eval (majorityAssignment φ) = false
```
nodes.statement: ∃ φ : CNF, φ.Satisfiable ∧ φ.eval (majorityAssignment φ) = false

nodes.title: P equals NP
nodes.spec:
P equals NP

The program's target: every language in NP has a polynomial-time decider.

```lean
PEqNP
```
nodes.statement: PEqNP
